recipes.name: Accidental Fish
ingredients_raw: 2 drops Louisiana-style hot sauce, or to taste

steps.text: Preheat the oven to 450 degrees F (230 degrees C).
Rub fillets with oil; transfer to a baking dish.
Bake in the preheated oven until fish flakes easily with a fork, about 20 minutes.

Meanwhile, melt butter in a saucepan over medium heat. Add lemon juice, garlic, and hot sauce; simmer for 1 minute. Add tomato and green onion; cook and stir until heated through. Spoon over fillets to serve.

raw_recipe.headline: Accidental Fish
raw_recipe.description: For this accidental fish recipe, baked Southern-style mahi mahi is topped with a simple butter-and-garlic sauce spiked with lemon juice and hot sauce.

review.reviewBody: This fish was excellent! I did make a few changes though. I put a little bit of extra virgin olive oil on the fish and salt and pepper before baking it. I turned the broiler on for about 2 minutes after the 20 minutes was up. I used half the butter and did not add tomato to the sauce. Instead, I added extra lemon juice and fresh parsley. This recipe is certainly a keeper!!!

Before I made this recipe I read the comments and I follow one tip which you broil atleast 2mins after it baked and sprinkle some pepper before you put the fish in the oven and I used cilantro instead of green onions and still taste great. I highly recommend this recipe its for keeps really great and yummy.

This recipe was great. So tasty! the lemon works well with the tomatoes and the mahi mahi was a delicious fish. The hot sauce added just a small kick of heat. Baked the fish at a lower temp and longer time just because the oil seemed to start burning at the beginning. also, seasoned the fish with salt, pepper and some chili powder before baking.

Simple and delicious! I used Barramundi which is a sustainable replacement for sea bass and other mild white fish. For 2 portions I used 2 T each of butter and Brummel & Brown lower fat butter. I microwaved the sauce because it was so hot in the kitchen. My fish cooked in 10 minutes because it was a thinner filet. I kept the other ingredients the same for the sauce and it was wonderful.
This will be a go-to staple in our kitchen!

I've made this several times now with mahi-mahi and cod -- it's a terrific weeknight dinner because it comes together so quickly. I use half butter/half EVOO and double the tomatoes and green onions. Tonight I'm trying it with one garlic clove and substituting ramps (wild leeks, which grow in our woods) for the green onions. You could probably use a dry white wine instead of the lemon juice. The sauce would be good over pasta without the fish!

This was delicious!!! I used 3 tilapia fillets, rubbed with olive oil, salt and peppered both sides. Squeezed 1/4 lemon over fish before baking as i didn't have any lemon pepper seasoning. Used all the butter the recipe calls for and thought it was perfect to pour on top of fish served on a bed of white rice. Didn't have the roma, squeezed 1/2 lemon in butter and an extra dash of Louisi hot sauce. squeezed remaining lemon over fish before adding lemon butter sauce. DE-LISH!!! I will be cooking fish more often.

Absolutely the best fish recipe we have ever made. Probably made it 25 times. The only minor improvement we made a while back is the addition of 1/4 cup of white wine to the sauce mixture and we simmer for about 15 minutes to thicken it a little.

This is a great recipe... So good and quick and easy. The only thing I changed was the pepper sauce... I used the Cholula Chipotle sauce for the smoky pepper flavor. I also only baked for 15 min. and it was perfect... White, moist and fell apart with the touch of a fork.. Thank you Becca!

The sauce was wonderful! Didn’t have green onions so I chopped a couple pieces of regular onion and let it simmer with the butter and garlic mixture. Didn’t use near as much butter though. Definitely need to use the tomatoes. Next time I’ll bake the fish like I usually do with butter, lemon and onion. Without the sauce it would have no flavor. Was really good with rice and the sauce, just couldn’t really taste the fish.
Worked great.Instead of Mahi Mahi,I used fresh large sardines.Dreged them in flour then fried them over med heat in a mixture of canola oil and butter.
It’s easy to prepare fast and yummy I made a few changes less amount of butter only 3 tablespoons and 1/4 cup of white wine
Absolutely yummy! One of our family favorites!
simple to prepare and yummy.

This is a very good receipe. I used mahi mahi and it was perfect. I also put salt and pepper on the fish before putting it in the oven. I used a vine ripe tomato as opposed to the roma tomato and I cut back on the butter. I'll be making this again.
without the hot sauce, tomato and onion.....it was still so simple and flavorful.

Delicious! and easy to make. I used Pollock instead of mahi-mahi. I will increase the sauce in the future with a little bit more tomato and some more hot sauce. It was milder than I was expecting but very delicious. I was afraid of the hot sauce, so I was easy on it. I served it over bed of rice. Yum!
Found some frozen Ahi Ahi fillets in my freezer that I grabbed from Aldi’s awhile ago. Never made it before so I was looking for an easy recipe. This was so easy and delicious!!!
So wonderful. We’re on Kauai & the fresh mahi-mahi was delicious cooked like this. Try it!
Wow, this was excellent and so easy to make! I made no alterations; perfect as it is!
it was bland. made my family think of chicken wings.
